# Volume 3 — Chapter VI In the Park

!!! note "Source text"
    Passages cited on the wiki pages link into this page. Only volumes at or before
    this page's cutoff are present.

“Girls, what do you plan to do with yourselves today?” inquired Cressida, entering Nell’s room suddenly one Saturday afternoon.
{: #nw-v03-c06-p0000 }

“We are taking a stroll through the park,” replied Nell. “I should remain indoors and complete my blouse. However, sewing is impossible for me on such a day. Something within the atmosphere penetrates my blood and creates a kind of magnificence in my soul. My fingers would jerk and I would stitch an uneven seam. Consequently, it is off to the park and the pines.”
{: #nw-v03-c06-p0001 }

“Is anyone besides Honora and you included in 'we'?”
{: #nw-v03-c06-p0002 }

“Indeed, Hugh and Wilfred are part of it, and it would bring us great pleasure to have you join as well.”
{: #nw-v03-c06-p0003 }

"However," Cressida uttered sorrowfully, "going means I must play third wheel, a role Cressida Lindsay has never experienced before."
{: #nw-v03-c06-p0004 }

“Indeed, novel occurrences expand one’s horizons. Join me, and you will find yourself capable of empathizing with every unfortunate individual forced to play third wheel frequently. However, where have all the sufferers gone?”
{: #nw-v03-c06-p0005 }

“Oh, I was weary of the lot of them and just could not be troubled with a single one today. Furthermore, I have been experiencing a slight sadness—merely a faint, fleeting light blue. My mood is not grave enough to warrant a deeper shade. Last week, I penned letters to Hector and Orlando. I placed the notes inside envelopes and wrote their addresses, yet I left them unsealed. Later that night, a peculiar event occurred. Namely, Hector would consider it amusing, whereas Orlando probably would not. Since I was in a rush, I grabbed what I assumed was Hector’s letter from its envelope and hastily added a postscript. Afterward, I posted both of the letters. Orlando’s response arrived for me this morning. Girls, I had written that postscript on his letter instead, and he was enraged. Naturally, he will recover from it—and it matters not to me if he fails to—yet it ruined my day. Consequently, I decided I would visit you darlings so you could brighten my spirits. Once the football season commences, I will not possess any free Saturday afternoons. Football is something I adore. I have acquired the most magnificent cap and sweater featuring stripes in the Wexcombe colors to don for the matches. Admittedly, from a slight distance I will resemble a moving barber’s pole. Are you aware that that Hugh of yours was chosen as Captain of the Freshman football team?”
{: #nw-v03-c06-p0006 }

“Indeed, he mentioned that to us yesterday night,” remarked Honora, noticing that a furious Nell refused to respond. “He visited alongside Wilfred. Having anticipated their arrival, we meticulously hid or removed all the cushions belonging to Miss Ada. The extremely intricate one featuring raised embroidery was dumped onto the ground in the corner behind its chair by me. I assumed its safety was guaranteed there. Yet, can you imagine? Wilfred Mott headed straight to that seat, spotted the cushion lying behind it, gravely pulled it out, and remained seated on it for the entire night. It became an absolute disaster of a cushion! Today, poor Miss Ada inquired of me, her expression remaining polite, yet expressing deep disappointment, why I had permitted someone to sit on it. My response to her was that I hadn’t—it resulted from fate joined with persistent Sloanish behavior, and I lacked the ability to defeat both together.”
{: #nw-v03-c06-p0007 }

“Miss Ada’s cushions are truly irritating me,” Nell remarked. “Seven days ago she completed a pair of new ones, packed tight and covered with embroidery to the extreme limits. Because there was no remaining spot lacking a cushion to place them, she lined them up against the wall on the landing of the stairs. They fall down during fifty percent of the time, and we trip on them whenever we navigate the stairs in pitch-blackness. Last Sunday, while Dr. Twiss offered a prayer for everyone subject to the dangers of the ocean, I privately inserted ‘and for everyone residing in homes where cushions receive an affection that is unwise and excessive!’ There! our preparations are complete, and I spot the boys approaching by way of Old St. John’s. Are you joining your fate with ours, Cressy?”
{: #nw-v03-c06-p0008 }

“Provided I am able to stroll alongside Honora and Wilfred, I will attend. Such an arrangement will render the chaperone role tolerable. Your Hugh is genuinely wonderful, Nell, yet what prompts his frequent company with Goggle-eyes?”
{: #nw-v03-c06-p0009 }

Nell went rigid. Wilfred Mott was not someone she particularly cared for; nevertheless, he belonged to Brierley, which meant no stranger had the right to mock him.
{: #nw-v03-c06-p0010 }

“Wilfred and Hugh have constantly been friends,” she stated distantly. “Wilfred is a good boy. His eyes are not his fault.”
{: #nw-v03-c06-p0011 }

“Forbidden to say so! Indeed he is! To receive the penalty of those very eyes, his past life must have contained a terrible deed. Today’s afternoon will bring Nonie and me great amusement through him. In his presence, we are going to mock him, completely beyond his awareness.”
{: #nw-v03-c06-p0012 }

Unquestionably, “the abandoned P’s,” to use Nell’s phrase, fulfilled their pleasant plans. Mott, however, remained happily unaware; he considered himself quite a dashing chap for strolling alongside a pair of such coeds, particularly Cressida Lindsay, who was the belle and beauty of the class. Nell would certainly be impressed by it. She was bound to realize that certain individuals recognized his true worth.
{: #nw-v03-c06-p0013 }

Hugh and Nell lagged slightly behind the rest of the group, taking pleasure in the quiet, peaceful charm of the autumn afternoon beneath the park's pine trees, along the ascending and winding path that encircled the harbor coast.
{: #nw-v03-c06-p0014 }

“Doesn’t the quietness in this place resemble a prayer?” asked Nell, looking up toward the luminous sky. “My affection for the pine trees is so great! The way they anchor their roots appears to reach into the ancient romance of every era. Finding solace in sneaking off occasionally to have a deep conversation with them brings such comfort. Being out in these woods continually fills me with joy.”
{: #nw-v03-c06-p0015 }

“‘Thus, captured within secluded peaks as if touched by a holy enchantment, their worries slip away from them just like needles brushed from a windy pine tree,’”
{: #nw-v03-c06-p0016 }

quoted Hugh.
{: #nw-v03-c06-p0017 }

“Our small aspirations appear quite insignificant by comparison, do they not, Nell?”
{: #nw-v03-c06-p0018 }

“If I were ever visited by a profound grief, I believe I would seek solace among the pine trees,” Nell remarked in a daydreamy tone.
{: #nw-v03-c06-p0019 }

“I wish that you are never visited by any severe grief, Nell,” uttered Hugh, unable to associate the concept of grief with the lively, happy girl at his side, ignorant that individuals capable of ascending to the loftiest peaks can likewise sink to the lowest abysses, and that those personalities that experience joy most intensely are the very ones that endure pain most acutely.
{: #nw-v03-c06-p0020 }

“However, there has to be—at some point,” Nell reflected. “Right now, life feels like a goblet of triumph pressed to my mouth. Nevertheless, it must contain a degree of gall—all cups do. One day, I will drink my share. Ah, I trust I will possess the strength and courage to face it. Furthermore, I pray it does not arrive as a result of my own wrongdoing. Are you mindful of Dr. Twiss’s remarks this past Sunday night—how the griefs bestowed by God brought consolation and power alongside them, whereas the griefs we inflicted upon ourselves, via foolishness or sinfulness, were immensely more difficult to endure? Still, we should not discuss grief on such an afternoon. It was created for the pure delight of existence, wasn’t it?”
{: #nw-v03-c06-p0021 }

“Nell, I would exclude all things except joy and delight from your existence if it were up to me,” Hugh stated with the particular voice that signaled “danger ahead.”
{: #nw-v03-c06-p0022 }

“If so, your choice would be most foolish,” Nell quickly retorted. “In my view, an existence cannot achieve true growth and completeness if it lacks all hardship and grief—even if we likely acknowledge this fact solely during times of relative ease. Hurry—our companions have reached the pavilion and are waving for us to join them.”
{: #nw-v03-c06-p0023 }

They gathered and sat in the small pavilion so they could observe a fall sunset composed of faint gold and intense crimson fire. Portmaris was situated to their left, with its spires and roofs appearing faint beneath a covering of violet smoke. The harbor was located to their right, acquiring shades of copper and rose while it spread outward toward the sunset. The water sparkled in front of them, silver gray and smooth as satin, and past it, clean shaven William’s Island emerged from the fog, protecting the town in the manner of a resolute bulldog. The signal of its lighthouse shone through the fog resembling a menacing star, which received a reply from a different one on the distant horizon.
{: #nw-v03-c06-p0024 }

“Have you ever beheld a location that appeared so formidable?” Cressida inquired. “I do not particularly desire William’s Island, yet I am certain that it would be unobtainable for me even if I wished for it. Observe the sentry positioned upon the peak of the fortification, directly next to the flag. Is he not the very image of a character who has emerged from a tale of romance?”
{: #nw-v03-c06-p0025 }

“Apropos of romance,” Honora remarked, “we’ve been searching for heather—though, naturally, we weren't able to locate any. I imagine the season is too far advanced.”
{: #nw-v03-c06-p0026 }

“Heather!” cried out Nell. “Does heather grow in America, then?”
{: #nw-v03-c06-p0027 }

“Across the entire continent, only two spots of it exist,” Cressy remarked, “this single one inside the park, and another located in Nova Scotia, though the exact place escapes my memory. A year saw the Black Watch, the renowned Highland Regiment, pitch camp on this site, and as the soldiers beat out their mattress straw during spring, heather seeds caught hold and grew.”
{: #nw-v03-c06-p0028 }

“Oh, how delightful!” said enchanted Nell.
{: #nw-v03-c06-p0029 }

“We could head back via Linden Avenue,” Hugh proposed. “It will allow us to view ‘the grand residences of the rich elite.’ Portmaris has no better street for living than Linden Avenue. Building there is restricted solely to millionaires.”
{: #nw-v03-c06-p0030 }

“Oh, do,” Cressy remarked. “Nell, I want to display a completely delightful small property to you. A millionaire did not construct it. Positioned as the initial site upon exiting the park, its development surely occurred when Linden Avenue remained a rural lane. Developed it was—never constructed! The residences along the Avenue fail to appeal to me. Their condition is overly new and full of plate glass. Yet this tiny location is divine—and as for its title—you must simply wait to behold it.”
{: #nw-v03-c06-p0031 }

As they strolled up the pine-fringed hill from the park, they spotted it. Situated right on the crest, at the point where Linden Avenue tapered off into an ordinary road, stood a small white frame house flanked by clusters of pines that extended their limbs in a protective manner over its low roof. Red and gold vines clad the home, with its green-shuttered windows peering out through them. A miniature garden, encircled by a low stone wall, lay in front of it. Even though it was October, the garden remained deeply fragrant with beloved, old-fashioned, unworldly flowers and shrubs—sweet may, southern-wood, lemon verbena, alyssum, petunias, marigolds and chrysanthemums. Leading from the gate to the front porch was a small brick walk arranged in a herring-bone pattern. The entire property appeared as if it could have been uprooted from a distant rural village; nevertheless, it possessed a quality that rendered its closest neighbor, the grand lawn-surrounded mansion of a tobacco king, remarkably unrefined, ostentatious, and vulgar in comparison. As Cressy said, it was the difference between being born and being made.
{: #nw-v03-c06-p0032 }

“It’s the most precious spot I’ve ever laid eyes on,” Nell stated with joy. “It causes one of my familiar, wonderfully strange pangs. It’s even sweeter and more unusual than the stone home belonging to Miss Rosalind.”
{: #nw-v03-c06-p0033 }

“I want you to pay particular attention to the name,” Cressy said. “See—encircling the archway above the gate, written in white lettering. ‘Tabby’s Place.’ Isn’t that hilarious? Particularly along this Avenue filled with Pinehursts, Elmwolds, and Cedarcrofts? ‘Tabby’s Place,’ no less! I absolutely love it.”
{: #nw-v03-c06-p0034 }

“Do you know who Tabby might be?” inquired Honora.
{: #nw-v03-c06-p0035 }

“I have learned that Tabby Linden is the name of the elderly woman who possesses it,” I remarked. “She resides in that place alongside her niece, and their residence there has spanned hundreds of years, give or take a few—perhaps slightly fewer, Nell. Overstatement is simply a creative surge of poetry. It has come to my knowledge that affluent people have attempted to purchase the property repeatedly—indeed, it commands a great sum today, as you are aware—yet ‘Tabby’ refuses to sell for any price whatsoever. Furthermore, a real apple orchard occupies the space behind the residence instead of a rear lawn—you will spot it once we move slightly further along—an actual apple orchard situated on Linden Avenue!”
{: #nw-v03-c06-p0036 }

“To-night my dreams will be of ‘Tabby’s Place,’” Nell remarked. “Why, it feels to me as though I were a part of it. I am curious whether there is any possibility that we will ever get a view of its interior.”
{: #nw-v03-c06-p0037 }

“It is not probable,” Honora remarked.
{: #nw-v03-c06-p0038 }

Nell gave a mysterious smile.
{: #nw-v03-c06-p0039 }

“No, the likelihood is low. Nevertheless, I hold the belief that it shall occur. A peculiar, eerie, unsettling sensation—term it a presentiment, should you wish—possesses me that ‘Tabby’s Place’ and my person will become even more familiar.”
{: #nw-v03-c06-p0040 }
